title: The Man Who Sold the Eiffel Tower

lines.tts: In 1925, a con man sold the Eiffel Tower. Then he came back and tried to sell it again.
lines.text: In 1925, a con man sold the Eiffel Tower. Then he came back and tried to sell it again.

lines.tts: Victor Lustig reads in the paper that the tower is rusting, and costs a fortune to fix.
lines.text: Victor Lustig reads in the paper that the tower is rusting, and costs a fortune to fix.

lines.tts: So he gets fake government letters printed, and calls himself a deputy director of the ministry.
lines.text: So he gets fake government letters printed, and calls himself a deputy director of the ministry.

lines.tts: He invites a group of scrap metal dealers to a secret meeting in a fancy Paris hotel.
lines.text: He invites a group of scrap metal dealers to a secret meeting in a fancy Paris hotel.

lines.tts: The government, he whispers, is selling the tower for scrap. But nobody can know.
lines.text: The government, he whispers, is selling the tower for scrap. But nobody can know.

lines.tts: One dealer, André Poisson, wants it more than anyone. He's new in town, and desperate to be a big shot.
lines.text: One dealer, André Poisson, wants it more than anyone. He's new in town, and desperate to be a big shot.

lines.tts: Then Lustig makes his best move. He confesses.
lines.text: Then Lustig makes his best move. He confesses.

lines.tts: He's a crooked official, his salary is tiny, and could Monsieur maybe help him out?
lines.text: He's a crooked official, his salary is tiny, and could Monsieur maybe help him out?

lines.tts: Poisson relaxes. A bribe? Now that's how real government works.
lines.text: Poisson relaxes. A bribe? Now that's how real government works.

lines.tts: He pays the bribe, and the money for the tower. Lustig grabs the cash and runs to Austria.
lines.text: He pays the bribe, and the money for the tower. Lustig grabs the cash and runs to Austria.

lines.tts: You see, a con is like a magic trick. People don't believe what you show them. They believe what they figure out themselves.
lines.text: You see, a con is like a magic trick. People don't believe what you show them. They believe what they figure out themselves.

lines.tts: And Poisson? He's so embarrassed, he never even calls the police.
lines.text: And Poisson? He's so embarrassed, he never even calls the police.

lines.tts: So Lustig comes back to Paris, and tries the exact same thing again. This time someone does call the police, and he escapes to America.
lines.text: So Lustig comes back to Paris, and tries the exact same thing again. This time someone does call the police, and he escapes to America.

lines.tts: Ten years later, he finally goes to prison. On Alcatraz. The one landmark he couldn't sell his way out of.
